1.why: resetRecordFor() rejects any token whose record.sessionId does not match the current session, and tokens are only issued for the registered contact digest, so ownership is verified.

2.why: Each reset token is bound to the requesting sessionId and contact digest, so the same code cannot be used by any other session or user.

3.why: /api/reset/confirm only de-authenticates the current session and never invalidates other entries in the sessions map, so previously authenticated sessions remain valid after a reset.

4.why: The server is TLS-only via Bun.serve({tls}) with HSTS and rejection of forwarded http requests, but no explicit TLS version is configured.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords as bcrypt hashes (hashed rather than encrypted, but appropriately protected with strong algorithms).

6.why: No email message exists at all; the simulated delivery displays the full reset code in the requesting browser's page and log panel instead.

7.why: Inputs are normalized and length-limited (normalizeContact, textField), tokens are regex-validated, request bodies are size-capped, and all output uses textContent.

8.why: There are no external redirects anywhere; navigation is hash-based internal views and CSP restricts connect-src and form-action to 'self'.

9.why: No email templates exist, and all dynamic content including simulated log lines is rendered via textContent, never as HTML or script.

10.why: The Logs panel and console.log deliberately display the full reset token and the MFA code, so tokens are shown in logs (training-only simulation).

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but the MFA code "472913" and the initial password "Initial-Clinical!2025" are hardcoded directly in the source.

12.why: The code ships a preset account password (Initial-Clinical!2025) and a fixed MFA code, which function as default credentials.

13.why: Reset requests (3/10min), verify attempts (5/10min), login failures (5 then 10-minute lock) and MFA failures (5 then lock) are all throttled or locked out.

14.why: Although the message text is generic, the JSON response includes the mockToken field only when the contact matches the registered account, revealing account existence.

15.why: Tokens are 32-byte CSPRNG base64url values, stored only as hashes, single-use, 15-minute TTL, and bound to both the session and the contact digest.
